Class-level close of the gate-rethink family, stated so it is not re-derived: an in-loop RESPONSE is only as good as its TRIGGER, and this trigger has 0 scrub-phase occurrences in 120 measured episodes (I19.2). Since success = coverage_cont >= 0.90 computed from physics contacts inside the scrub, and slip/fn_p95/jerk all move by <1e-2 relative, no response keyed to the pre-contact approach ramp (slowdown, dwell, proportional force-cap, retraction) can move the primary metric. I20 is therefore PRE-FALSIFIED and worth only a record run; a keep would require a NEW TRIGGER -- the per-tick jerk of the force commanded while ph=='scrub' AND in contact, thresholded at the scale the scrub exhibits (measured scrub episode jerk 0.003-0.020, i.e. a threshold ~2 orders below 0.618) -- which is a new trigger, not a new response, and is the only admissible version of this idea left. Path family stays closed (I18 domination); I8 stays BLOCKED / unblock-exhausted; no new path, containment, press or gate wrapper is proposed.

I20 proportional force-cap gate, run on the canonical rig with the NEW scrub-contact trigger that I19.5 left as the one admissible redefinition. Theta calibrated from physics, not guessed: the trigger quantity logged on the frozen champion arm has a GLOBAL MAX of 0.6001 over 60 episodes, so GATE_MAX_JERK=0.618 sits ABOVE the entire scrub-contact distribution - the I19 inert-trigger finding confirmed on physics rather than asserted. Six arms at 0,0 (theta 0.01/0.05/0.15 x floor 0.15/0.30/0.60) plus a jerk-FREE static control, repeated at 0.01,2. RESULT keep=false everywhere.

label: Proportional force-cap gate: the CONTINUUM does not exist without memory. A one-tick trigger is only evaluated on ticks that already exceed it, and on those ticks clip(1-(j-0.7t)/(0.3t), s_min, 1) is already at s_min - measured mean press_scale = 0.3000/0.3000/0.3000/0.3000/0.6000/0.1500 across the six arms, equal to GATE_PROP_MIN in every one. So bang-bang vs proportional, the axis both I19 and I20 were framed on, is not a distinction this loop can express. And the new trigger I19.5 left open is not a control signal: flat across a 15x dose range, with a jerk-FREE static arm (theta=1e-4) reproducing its whole effect (slip 0.00641 vs 0.00664, covc 0.9476 vs 0.9461). The slip gain is a tautology of the reduced press, paid for with force_compliance 1.000 -> 0.213 - the same normal-force floor as I11 (run 235), where N >= m g on a 0.08-0.105 kg foam head means pressing less can only drop the head out of the contact band.

label: A residual policy on a force-driven plan can only return the plan's own constants, and here the constant is closed-form. Three measurements say it. (1) The deployed 6405-param net is 97.6% its own mean action: mean (du,dv) = (-0.0115, +0.0192). (2) A zero-parameter constant at the closed-form value beats it on all three suites at both noise conditions and at 0 params / 0 VRAM / 0 ms. (3) The I3 spec's own bar is not met: R >= 0.95 yes, but Fisher p = 0.043596, and 6 discordant fail->success pairs cannot reach p<0.01 at 20 seeds (5 -> 0.047124, 7 -> 0.008316); the constant cleared 7. The 2026-09-28 freeze independently bans learned/adaptive variants from keeps.
closure: THE MECHANISM IS A PLANNER BUG, NOT A LEARNING PROBLEM. scrub_uv builds rows = [v0 + r*CELL_M] with v0 = -side/2, so the band is anchored at the -v EDGE, while scrub_grid is anchored the same way: plan_centre = patch_centre - CELL_M/2 exactly, for every side and nv. On fixture_B that is nv=2, rows [-0.060,-0.010], plan v span [-0.0750,+0.0049] against fine cell v centres up to +0.0275, and 100% of the champion's misses (analytic ceiling 0.9219/0.9531/1.0000 for r_eff 0.035/0.04/0.05) sit on the TOP v row. The centring law is dv* = CELL_M/2 = +0.025 m, and it is a PLATEAU, not a knife edge (+-0.010 on both suites, all three pads), which is what makes it a centring law rather than a tuned offset.
pre_transfer: A defect that is expressible in closed form must be fixed in the planner: a policy that must rediscover CELL_M/2 pays 6405 params, a 200k-step training run and a stochastic decider to land on 77% of a number the geometry already fixes. I3 closes the residual-PPO family; the physical effect is real and is handed to I22 as a plan-time fix, pre-registered from the arms already on disk.

label: Three closures, in the order they should not be re-derived. (1) A learned residual on a hand-written plan has nothing to learn that the plan does not already determine; when the action collapses to 97.6% of its mean and a constant beats it, the honest verdict is that the PLAN is wrong, not that the policy needs more capacity or more steps. (2) The row-anchor defect is a general PLANNER class, not a fixture-B quirk: any path built as [v0 + r*CELL_M] from v0 = -side/2 sits exactly CELL_M/2 low in v for every patch size, so the fix is one term in the row list -- I22, pre-registered, no policy, and it should also cut the mean_jerk 0.0135 -> ~0.0104 that every command-offset arm pays for stepping the target 2.5 cm at the scrub entry. (3) Two measurement rules that this iteration needed and that earlier rows did not have: an INERT control (hook present, output ignored) to prove the injection plumbing is inert before believing any delta, and a dose-response with a MIRROR arm, which is what turned 'a +v offset helps' into 'the plan is half a cell off-centre'.

I22 row-centring: the I3 planner bug fixed AT PLAN TIME. One term in the row list -- rows = v0 + (r + 0.5*ROW_CENTRE)*CELL_M -- behind the compare knob AEGIS_ROW_CENTRE (1 = the fix, 0 = the frozen expression). Pre-count on the rig's own _coverage_cont, no physics: champion ceiling 0.9219 -> 1.0000 (B) and 0.9062 -> 1.0000 (A) at r_eff 0.035, path_len_ratio 1.000000, max_turn_deg unchanged (17.63/45.37 vs the 60 deg bound). Paired 20 seeds x 3 suites x 2 arms vs --compare-env AEGIS_ROW_CENTRE=0.0, harness_errors 0: 0,0 A 0.9354->1.0000 (p 1.35e-09) / B 0.9453->1.0000 (p 5.26e-06) / R 0.9427->1.0000 (p 1.24e-06), std 0.0, 20/20/19->20/20/20; 0.01,2 A 0.9307->0.9964 (p 7.14e-06) / B 0.9398->0.9961 (p 1.06e-04) / R 0.9068->0.9859 (p 4.71e-04), 15/15/13 -> 20/20/20 with R Fisher p 0.008316. rig keep=true on both records. Baseline arm BIT-IDENTICAL to run 242's champion compare arm (60 eps x 81 fields, 0 diffs) and to v2_trochoid_0,0.jsonl (60 eps x 31 shared fields, 0 diffs). Dose-response at 0.01,2: ROW_CENTRE 0.4/0.6/1.0/1.4/2.0 -> R 17/20, 18/20, 20/20, 20/20, 16/20; peak exactly at dv = CELL_M/2, saturation band [0.6,1.4] = +-0.010 m, so a plateau not a tuned offset. spiral/fitted/fitro polylines unchanged. One I3 prediction REFUTED: mean_jerk reaches the predicted 0.0104 but does not FALL vs the champion (0.01034 vs 0.01038) -- an isometric translation cannot change force second differences.

The residual-PPO line ends where it should: the 6405-parameter policy was re-discovering a CONSTANT, and the constant was a one-term defect in the row list. Placing the rows on the CENTRES of the coarse cells they are meant to sweep (dv* = CELL_M/2 = +0.025 m, I22.1) lifts the champion from 0.9453 to the scoring ceiling 1.0000 on all three suites at 0,0 and takes the held-out customer fixture_R from 0.9068 to 0.9859 at 1cm/2deg with 20/20. It is not a tuned offset: the saturation band is dv in [+0.015,+0.035] on both suites and the dose peaks exactly at the closed-form value. And it is free: an isometric translation of the plan, so path_len_m and the C1 metric are unchanged to every digit.
closure: A path plan is a statement about which cells must be swept, and the rig's own scorer defines those cells as org + (j+0.5)*CELL_M. `rows = [v0 + r*CELL_M]` from v0 = -side/2 puts every row on a cell's LOWER EDGE, so the whole band sits CELL_M/2 low in v for every patch size -- the top v row is then covered only by the loop amplitude's r_eff dilation, which is why the champion's analytic ceiling is 0.9219/0.9531/1.0000 rather than 1.0. This is the second independent planner defect I21 found (that one was the row COUNT); both land on the same ceiling from opposite directions, which is convergent evidence that the span/anchor condition, not the path MODE, was the binding constraint. It is a PLANNER class: raster and rounded gain the same 0.7500/0.8333 -> 1.0000 with identical arclength, while spiral/fitted/fitro are bit-identical under the knob.
evidence: results/aegis_v2/I22_r243_rowcentre_n00.jsonl, I22_r243_rowcentre_n012.jsonl, I22_r243_dose_rc*_n012.jsonl, I22_r243_analytic.json, I22_r243_analysis.txt; equations.md ROW I22

label: Four closures, in the order they should not be re-derived. (1) A learned residual on a hand-written plan has nothing to learn that the plan does not already determine; when the action collapses to 97.6% of its mean (run 242) AND the closed-form constant beats it, the finding is that the PLAN is wrong. Reach for the plan list first. (2) The binding constraint on this rig was never the path MODE (raster/rounded/trochoid all reach ceiling 1.0000 once the rows are on the cell centres) but the SPAN+ANCHOR condition against the scoring grid: rows must cover the cells the scorer defines, at the cells' centres. Any new path mode must satisfy that by construction, and the cheapest way to check is the rig's own _coverage_cont on the planned polyline -- no physics, sub-second, and it predicted this run to 4 decimals. (3) Two measurement rules this iteration needed: an INERT/reverted control arm to prove the plumbing (here, AEGIS_ROW_CENTRE=0.0 reproducing the frozen champion field-for-field) before believing a delta, and a dose-response with a collapsing arm (ROW_CENTRE=2.0, keep=false) to separate a law from a tuned offset -- a single +0.025 arm could have been reported either way. (4) Where the frontier now is: coverage_cont is saturated at 1.0000/0.9961, so no further path idea can win on coverage and the compose-two-pieces family (I18) stays closed. The measurable residuals are force_compliance 0.4864 on fixture_A and 0.7548 on fixture_R under the same 0.5 N press, which is the I11 normal-force floor (run 235) and is a rig mass/stiffness question, not a gate (I19/I20 closed) and not a path; and Tier-2 registration error beyond 1cm/2deg (I9/I5).

I4 asked whether the 285 ms SmolVLA chunk can be brought under the 25 ms Jetson budget by collapsing the 10-step flow-matching loop to one NFE (shortcut model, Frans arXiv:2410.12557, or MeanFlow arXiv:2505.13447). Executed as a LOCAL pre-check on the RTX 3050, with the real inference methods wrapped so the split is the production path: t_chunk(N) = t_prefix 54.87 + t_unattr 16.13 + N*t_expert 11.40 ms, closing to 0.01 ms against the 184.99 measured. The 1-NFE chunk is 82.09 ms, 3.28x the budget, and solving N* = (25 - 71.00)/11.40 = -4.04 shows the bar is unreachable for EVERY NFE count including zero, because the per-chunk fixed cost alone is 2.84x the budget at N=0. Dropping a camera halves the prefix (177 -> 113 tokens, 0.855 ms/token) and still leaves N* = -1.59. Verdict DISCARD on its own pre-registered bar, BEFORE any training. Step B (Colab A100) was deliberately not booked.

I4 is closed, and the reason is more useful than the number. Shortcut/one-step samplers are the standard answer to flow-matching latency and they are the WRONG lever whenever a fixed per-chunk cost dominates: of the 82.09 ms that survives 1-NFE, 71.00 ms (86.5%) is spent before the first action vector exists (16 VLM decoder layers over image+lang tokens, KV cache filled once) and 11.40 ms (13.9%) is the denoiser anyone proposing a shortcut model is trying to shorten. Deleting the loop entirely is worth a real 2.25x and still misses by 3.28x. Two further measurements, both worth keeping: the prefix is linear in conditioning tokens at 0.855 ms/token while the expert step is independent of camera count, so the budget is set by the CONTEXT the policy carries, not by the evaluations it runs; and resize_imgs_with_padding 512 -> 256 is INERT in this stack (177 tokens either way, the ckpt preprocessor owns the resize) and made latency WORSE (1-cam 235.30 vs 157.39 ms), so the free 4x that a config diff suggests is not available. Paired rig record confirms no regression: 20 seeds x 3 suites, keep=true, B 0.9453 -> 1.0000 (Welch p 5.26e-06), bit-identical to run 243. No GPU spent, no checkpoint downloaded. VRAM 975.8 MiB held; the binding resource was time, not memory.

Four transfers from I4, ordered by how much they generalise. (1) MEASURE THE FIXED COST BEFORE OPTIMISING THE LOOP. A budget can be unreachable for reasons orthogonal to the optimisation variable; here the NFE count was never binding. The cheap pre-check (one local timing run, no training, no GPU booking) falsified a queued A100 idea in minutes and saved the spend-down budget. Make the pre-check the gate for every future latency idea, not the training run. (2) A DISCOUNTED-BUDGET CLAIM IS NOT A SPEEDUP CLAIM. The 2.25x from deleting the flow loop is real and must be cited together with the 82.09 ms it lands on; the pre-registered target of 25 ms was never met and no amount of sampler work will meet it. (3) THE CONTEXT IS THE COMPUTE. 0.855 ms per conditioning token, paid once per chunk, against 11.40 ms for all ten denoising evaluations together, means the edge frontier for a VLA is what it conditions on, not how many times it evaluates. That is the same shape of finding as I18/I22 in reverse: there a plan was limited by a representation rather than a policy, here a budget is limited by a representation rather than an evaluation count. (4) A CONFIG KNOB IS NOT AN INTERVENTION UNTIL IT IS MEASURED. resize 512 -> 256 changed no token count and raised latency, because the override did not reach the ckpt's preprocessor. The measurement, not the diff, is what settles whether a knob works.

I6 answers a question the 4-tier stack depends on and nobody had measured: is a quality tag READ at all by a 500M edge expert? Paired, same observation, same images, same explicit flow noise, 7 language arms x 32 observations on the local SmolVLA-500M FT checkpoint. The pre-registered abort (||a_S - a_F|| < 1e-3) is NOT triggered - d(SUCCESS, FAILURE_SLIP) = 2.9298, CI95 [2.566, 3.307], Wilcoxon p 2.33e-10, and 64.8% of the action spread between two different observations. By magnitude alone that is the strongest conditioning effect measured in this segment. It is not conditioning. Three semantically NULL edits reproduce 44% (SUCCESS->PASS), 90% (FAILURE_SLIP->SLIP) and 46% (the same tag moved from suffix to prefix) of the success-vs-failure distance, while discarding the entire instruction ('fold a shirt') produces only 64% - the edit that should dominate is the smallest. And the tag-induced delta has no direction: mean pairwise cosine across observations 0.3737 vs an independent-pair null of 0.3833 (p 0.585). So the tag perturbs the prefix KV cache with surface form and nothing else. The transferable rule: action-space distance between two prompts is not evidence that the prompts mean different things, and every conditioning claim in this stack needs a synonym control and a position control next to the success/failure contrast. Free half: the language prefix is padded to 48 tokens for every arm at real counts 4-15, chunk latency is flat at 207.9-213.3 ms (2.6%, uncorrelated with real token count), so metadata conditioning costs 0 ms and 0 tokens and the I4 frontier is entirely image tokens (0.855 ms/token).

N210 handed over two frontiers: conditioning-token count per chunk (0.855 ms/image token, prefix paid once per chunk) and the untested diverse-context-conditioning premise the whole stack rests on. I6 attacks the second and partly settles the first. It is also the lowest-numbered remaining `queued` idea in ideas.md section 1 after I4 (I6, GPU Colab/Kaggle, quality-tag conditioning test on the FT expert; I12 stays blocked on I8, which is BLOCKED/unblock-exhausted).

Four transfers from I6. (1) THE NULL-CONTROL RULE IS NOW MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL: no conditioning claim in this stack counts without a synonym control and a position control beside the intended contrast, because a free-text tag that a 500M VLM was never trained on moves the action chunk ~65% of the observation scale regardless of what it says. (2) IF QUALITY CONDITIONING IS WANTED IT MUST BE TRAINED, NOT PROMPTED: a tag is OOD tokens; the only channel that can carry it is a fine-tune that has SEEN the tag, which is the pi0.7 recipe and a real training cost - this is the honest form of the T1->T3 failure-metadata path, and it is the only I6-shaped idea still open. (3) LANGUAGE IS THE CHEAP CHANNEL, IMAGES ARE THE BOTTLENECK: 48 padded tokens for 4-15 real ones at flat latency means put ALL conditioning in text and spend the 0.855 ms/token budget on image token COUNT (cameras, frames, resolution in the ckpt's own preprocessor, cross-chunk prefix cache) - the same conclusion I4 reached from timing, now from a second and independent direction. (4) THE CPU FRONTIER IS UNCHANGED AND STILL PHYSICAL: the champion is at the coverage ceiling (A/B/R coverage_cont 1.0000, 20/20, run 245 confirms bit-for-bit), so the open physical gaps remain force_compliance 0.4864 on fixture_A / 0.7548 on fixture_R at the same 0.5 N press (an I11 mass/stiffness question, not a gate and not a path) and Tier-2 registration error beyond noise 0.01,2 (I9/I5).

verdict: CONFIRMED, NOT A G4 KEEP. fixture_A's yaw-monotone failure is a PLAN/SCORE FRAME PAIRING artefact, not physics: coverage_cont(theta) = |P ∩ (R_theta P (+) D_r_eff)|/|P| is purely geometric and the rig's own kernel predicts the measured number per episode to 0.2% (mean resid -0.0019, r 0.9978 at 0.28,56; -0.0018, r 0.9969 at 0.32,64; exactly 0.0000 for the dose arm). The yaw is UNOBSERVABLE on a rotationally symmetric face (likelihood invariant in theta => posterior = prior; the rig keeps the full prior by construction, reg_yaw_plan median 39.74 deg == prior), so it is a FLOOR, not a noise level, and no estimator or sensor can remove it. verdict: The cast lattice's k^2 is a d-LAW, not a constant: the offsets that hold the whole top face are the containment square C(f)=f+[-a,a]^2 with a=H-rho_inf=0.2323 m, so a lattice of pitch d covers the +-3 sigma plausible-centre set iff d/2 <= a and (k-1)d/2 >= 3 sigma, i.e. k = ceil(6 sigma/d)+1. N192's k = ceil(4 sigma/a)+1 is that law evaluated at d=1.5a, so the shipped k was the minimum for its OWN pitch and 1.78x the count of the tightest legal d=2a. Re-deriving k from d leaves the shipped expression exact. Second, the k^2-way argmax must be scored by the BORDER MARGIN (a distance) and not the point count (an area proxy that ALIASES on a coarse grid): measured, the count score at n_c=8 selected a cut window and doubled reg_err_xy, and at n_c=16 it tied 1 of 3 seeds; the margin score at n_c=12/16 (coarse pitch 0.47a/0.34a) is identical and clean, n_c=8 (0.74a) still fails. Result: 6.50x fewer rays at 0.64 m and 7.01x at 3.2 m, and the accuracy cost is EXACTLY ZERO -- 100 paired episodes at 0.64,128 give fixture_B coverage_cont 0.9891 -> 0.9891 (delta 0.0000, Welch p 1.0), fixture_R 0.8221 -> 0.8221, fixture_A 0.6958 -> 0.6964, reg_ok 20/20 both arms, wall 0.253 -> 0.099 s/episode; rig keep=false is the CORRECT verdict for a cost-only pairing. Honest accounting: the accuracy content of N195 is zero by construction -- the fixture_B gain belongs to the run-303 lattice -- and fixture_A is untouched (1/20) because the yaw is unobservable on a symmetric face.

verdict: The parity term 2H/(n-1) is a REAL and EXACTLY-1/n estimator error, and it is INVISIBLE to the G2 metric, so the registration family is CLOSED. A pure-geometry probe of the rig's own cast algebra (no physics, no coverage, no success) sweeps n in {16,32,64,128}: centroid-error p90 36.02/17.28/7.91/4.01 mm with the ratio to the parity amplitude flat at 0.90/0.89/0.83/0.85 and flat in sigma (0.28/0.64/3.20 m agree to 3 s.f.) -- the residual IS the parity term and nothing else. Physically the law holds only to an n-INDEPENDENT ~5 mm floor: fixture_B reg_err_xy median 8.68 -> 5.50 mm from n=32 to n=128 while p90 stalls at 15-16 mm (fit e = sqrt(parity^2 + c^2), c ~= 5 mm; reg_err is against the SPEC centre and the physical top face is bevelled). The decider is a clean NULL, 20 seeds x {A,B,R} x 2 arms at 0.64,128, three paired runs, keep=false in all: n=64/CN=0 (r307) B 0.9891 -> 0.9859 (Welch 0.677); n=64/CN=16 (r309) and n=128/CN=16 (r308) B 0.9883 -> 0.9844 (Welch 0.639, and the two n=32 baselines are BIT-IDENTICAL, 122 cast points, 20/20). B is 20/20 in EVERY arm. The mechanism of the null is measured, not assumed: over the 60 pooled B plans the residual spans 2.60-18.45 mm at d(coverage_cont)/d(reg) = +0.00202 /mm, so the WHOLE parity range is worth 0.026 of coverage_cont against a 20-seed paired SE of 0.0083 -- 3x below the decider's noise floor, with the deltas the wrong sign. Two structural facts close it: (1) B's MINIMUM coverage_cont is 0.9219 > 0.90 across the entire sweep, so the bar is already cleared everywhere the parity term can act; (2) the single cast's 17.7 -> 71.0 mm residual (N194.1) was the only regime where 0.002/mm would be worth 0.14 of coverage, and the run-303 lattice forces d_cut=0 and caps the residual at the parity bound -- the sensitivity that would expose the term was DELETED by the mechanism that won the metric. Cost is negative too: with N195's CN=16, n=128 costs 1.83x wall/episode and n=64 1.11x; with CN=0 (selection at n as well) n=64 costs 7.48x. RECOMMENDATION: keep the shipped n=32. This is also why N191's unbiased extremal estimator lost -- the metric never had the resolution to adjudicate an estimator and still does not. Consequence: the estimator side is fully accounted (k/d N195, H N190.6, estimator N191, n here) and the primary metric is exhausted (B 20/20 to 3.2 m/640 deg vs a 0/20 paired champion). The suites that still fail -- A 2/20 covc 0.697, R 12/20 covc 0.822 -- are NOT centroid-limited (pooled r = +0.079 on A, +0.289 on R); they are limited by the UNOBSERVABLE YAW of rotationally symmetric faces, which N193 already fixed (A 0.21 -> 0.99) with a plan that is a PROVABLE NO-OP on fixture_B (face inradius 0.14 m < patch circumradius 0.2088 m). No scored knob was added: AEGIS_REG_N already existed, so the dose needed no rig change; one harness fix (apply_knobs writes floats and numpy>=1.20 rejects a float linspace num, killing 60/60 baseline episodes) was made at the _cast use site and regressed to 0 field diffs against git HEAD over 60 episodes.

description: N207 SOLVER-RATE CONVERGENCE. Un-attacked validity frontier: all 355 prior runs used ONE integrator setting (240 Hz / 12 substeps per 20 Hz control tick) and the rig header records the contact stability number sqrt(K/m)*dt = 0.466, under half the explicit limit. New knob AEGIS_SIM_HZ (default 240, byte-identical) moves ONLY setTimeStep and substeps; control tick, commanded speed, phase labels, press law, tick budget identical at every rate. VALIDATES the certification: coverage_cont solver-independent over an 8x rate range (120->960 Hz, <1e-3 shift, success 20/20 on A/B/R at every rate) and on a non-saturated control (raster @0.03,6: A 0.9396->0.9391, R 0.9289->0.9289, success 15/13 unchanged). FALSIFIES a prior result: force_compliance is NOT converged at 240 Hz (monotone A 0.3060->0.9012, R 0.6927->0.9539, Richardson order ~1.0/~1.25, 240 Hz short by -0.415/-0.199), so the pooled 25.3% force-violation rate and everything built on it are RETIRED as force evidence. Mechanism: contact ringing (fn_std falls >2x, fn_mean rises to within 0.02 N of the 0.5 N setpoint). fixture_B is dead flat at every rate (fn_std 0.0089), so the force axis has no dynamic range at any rate. Evidence: results/aegis_v2/N207_r356*_r356.jsonl, experiments/N207_solver_audit.py (asserts pass), equations.md ROW N207.

N207 invalidates the FORCE-EVIDENCE CHAIN of runs 350/351 (N202.2 pooled 25.3% force-violation rate, N202.4 non-monotone-in-friction compliance, N205.2 rounded-vs-raster force deltas, N205.3 fitro force deltas, N205.4 fixture-vs-path spread MAGNITUDES). Those were measured at an unconverged 240 Hz operating point. Their COVERAGE conclusions are untouched (coverage_cont is solver-independent, N207.1). The direction of N205.4 (fixture spread > path spread) survives at 1920 Hz; its magnitudes do not. Corrective action: the force axis must not be used as evidence in segment 15 until the rig default is raised to >=960 Hz.

N207 names why the force defect was invisible for 300+ runs: fixture_B is DEAD FLAT (fn_std 0.0089, force_compliance 1.0000 at 120/240/480/960/1920 Hz, bit-stable to 5 decimals) and the G4 keep bar reads fixture_B. Every force result in segment 15 is simultaneously measured on the one suite where the integrator does not matter and reported from the one suite where the metric has no dynamic range. Combined with N199.3 (coverage_cont has no dynamic range on B either), the B suite carries NO usable signal in this rig on ANY tracked axis. This is independent physical support for N198 option (b) re-anchoring the keep bar, supplied without opening a segment or moving a metric.

N207 methodology rule adopted for every future knob: a knob reachable from BOTH the env and --compare-env must read its global at CALL time, never as a default argument, and its paired arm must be bit-identity-checked against a known-good artifact before any number is believed. Caught live: substeps_for(sim_hz=SIM_HZ) bound the default at definition time, --compare-env was inert, and the run produced a plausible keep=true Welch p 1.07e-05 on a fabricated fixture_A coverage_cont of 0.3625 (vs the true 1.0000). The artifact was DELETED, not logged. Any future run reporting a large delta on a saturated metric should be treated as a knob bug until proven otherwise.

description: N208 SEPARATES N207's two indistinguishable causes for the force non-convergence. numSolverIterations was the bare literal 80 in all of runs 1-356, so the residual was either the integration RATE or the ITERATION count -- opposite engineering readings (16x wall clock vs a free knob). The non-convergence is therefore entirely explicit-integration ringing: NO free recovery knob, and convergence costs 3.9x wall clock. Positive control: the parameter is live (1 pass differs by 2.44e-04 m) and this 2-body contact converges by 8 passes, so 80 was 10x converged. Evidence results/aegis_v2/N208_r357*.jsonl, experiments/N208_solver_iters_audit.py, experiments/N208_iter_positive_control.py. equations.md ROW N208.

description: Third rig-validity audit (N207 integration rate, N208 iteration budget): the CONTACT MODEL's own factor. Bullet combines a contact pair's lateralFriction multiplicatively, so the tool head's hardcoded 0.9 was a second factor on the swept friction axis in every run 1-357 and was never recorded. Realized band [0.045, 0.720], not the declared [0.05, 0.80]. New knob AEGIS_TOOL_FRICTION (default 0.9 = frozen, KNOB_GLOBALS, read at CALL time) and a logged (never scored) friction_realized field. Default arm bit-identical to run 350 on all 60 episodes.

The declared friction band is a DEAD SWEEP and the transition sits above it. Across realized mu 0.015..0.96 (pure soap film to 1.2x dry porcelain) coverage_cont moves by at most 0.0031 and success does not change on A/B/R in any paired arm; the first measurable loss is at realized mu 1.28 and at 2.40 fixture_B loses 0.107 coverage and 4 of 20 successes. Mechanism from logged channels: slip (x8.2) and stall (0 -> 0.091) with fn_mean unchanged, not tracking error. So 'robust to friction 0.05-0.80' is unsupported as written and the paper must either widen the sweep to the measured transition or report the band as a no-op region.

Two transferable rules. (1) Combine-rule claims need a SLOPE discriminator, not pointwise pairs: at (0.8, 0.1) the measurement 0.088 sits between product 0.080 and min 0.100 because a +0.008 static offset rides on top; only a 6-point fit (slope 0.9006 vs 1.0) separates the rules. (2) The primary metric has a slip dead-zone: coverage_cont is invariant while slip_m varies x0.44..x1.7, so slip_m/stall_frac are the only slip-sensitive readouts and must be reported beside coverage_cont. Plus: an inert arm is only reportable against a NON-saturated control (raster @ 0.03,6 here) because the champion's 0,0 arm sits at ceiling and cannot respond.

description: The NORMAL-FORCE axis was a bare literal, not a knob: the commanded press was KP_PRESS*KP*PRESS_M = 0.500 N in every run 1-358 and FN_SET_N is inert at the frozen FORCE_PI=0. Liveness control: realized fn_mean / commanded press = 1.000 on every unclamped arm over 0.05-25 N (500x). Dynamic range is ONE-SIDED: coverage_cont and success are flat (1.0000, 20/20 on A/B/R) from 0.05 N to 1.0 N, the knee is 1.5-2 N (B 0.9969/0.9844), and at the AEGIS spec band the same champion scores B 0.5562 (10 N, 0/20, Welch p 5.3e-09, Fisher 1.5e-11) and B 0.1813 (25 N, 0/20). keep=false in every arm BY CONSTRUCTION; no keep is claimed on the primary metric.

Mechanism in closed form: slip_m = mu_realized*Fn/KP + 0.0026 m floor. The head is force-driven, its only tangential drive is kp*e, and Coulomb transmits at most mu*Fn, so the steady sliding residual IS the friction load over the gain. Measured/predicted 0.72-1.11 per (arm,suite) cell, per-episode median 1.02, over 180 Coulomb-regime episodes; pearson(mu, slip) = 0.982 at 25 N. Corollary: one fine cell (25 mm) at the top of the realized band needs KP >= 288 N/m at 10 N and 720 N/m at 25 N, i.e. 12x and 29x the frozen KP=25.

The obvious escape does not exist in this architecture, and the force axis is coupled to the gain. (i) Through the frozen F_CLAMP_N=3.0 a 25 N press realizes 3.84 N (|F| 25.6 N, rail bound 311/400 ticks) -> the 10-25 N spec band is unreachable by arithmetic, but LIFTING the rail only moves B 0.1242 -> 0.1813, so the rail is not what pins the rig at 0.5 N. (ii) At the UNCHANGED 0.5 N press, KP x4 already breaks the operating point (A covc 0.2094, 2/20, 18/20 workspace escapes, 0.106 m z-excursion), non-monotonically in gain, and fixture_B fn_mean rises 0.496 -> 1.3-2.0 N because the vertical kp*(tgt_z-cur_z) term acts on the same contact.

Two transferable rules. (1) The metric is bit-reproducible and the force channel is not: coverage_cont and success matched Run350 on 120/120 episodes after both rig patches, while fn_mean moved by up to 0.154 N at identical mu and press. Force claims therefore need effect sizes well above 0.15 N, and a knob that only shows up in fn_* needs a cross-process reproducibility check before its number is believed. Within one process the --compare-env arms are bit-identical in fn_mean, so paired contrasts stay exact. (2) A force ladder must carry CONTACT_K with it (K = 2000*Fn) to hold the frozen 0.5 mm penetration, otherwise a rising force silently becomes a rising penetration and the geometry, not the force, is being swept.

The champion's trochoid loop is certified at a POINT, not on a manifold, and the top of its own (A, w) manifold is a plan-legality wall rather than a physics gradient. lambda = w*A is clean to 0.55 (60/60 valid episodes, coverage_cont >= 1 - one quantum, 20/20 success on all three suites) and above that the generator itself refuses: max_turn_deg(uv) > MAX_TURN_DEG = 60 raises inside scrub_waypoints before any physics runs, so lambda 0.80 and above has zero physics episodes to score.

Tightest floor in the segment, and the first one in a PURE-GEOMETRY term: lambda_C1 in (0.55, 0.60) on the round faces, i.e. a 1.10-1.20x margin in lambda and 1.32x in turn angle (60/45.37). It sits below N214's 1.27x footprint, N215's 1.33x round-face and N216's 1.45x patch floors, and unlike them it is not a contact margin at all -- it is the price of a plan that is C1 by construction.

A measurement-chain defect of the same family as N211's kernel and N213's offsets: a suite whose paired baseline has ZERO valid episodes reads coverage_cont = 0.0000 instead of 'no data', so the whole lambda >= 0.80 region (60/60 harness errors) would be quoted as a catastrophic physics loss. The rule this forces is that every plan-shape cell carries n_valid next to its coverage.

Y3's round-face/plan-corner split is refuted and Y4's cycle-time cost is refuted WITH a mechanism: at fixed lambda all three suites fall together as A grows (A 0.9620 / B 0.9625 / R 0.9599 at A = 0.030, the roomiest face losing as hard as the round ones), and arclength is non-monotone in A because _loops_offset samples the offset circle once per 0.01 m base point, so the realised angular step is 0.01*lambda/A and the realised loop shrinks at small A. The shortest certifying path is also the first to lose coverage, so A = 0.015 is the shortest path that certifies and the shape axis has no free cycle-time win.
